turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for calling the medical information department of Rising Pharma Holdings. You are speaking with Jenna. This call may be recorded for quality and training purposes. How may I help you?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hi. Um. I'm calling because my dad passed away, and the hospital said one of his medicines might have had something to do with it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm so sorry for your loss. I will help you with that. Before I proceed, could you please help me with your name and telephone number?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure. My name is Linda. L I N D A.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And your last name, please?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Brennan. B as in Bravo, R as in Romeo, E as in Echo, N as in November, N as in November, A as in Alpha, N as in November.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. That's Linda Brennan, B R E N N A N. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And the telephone number, Ms. Brennan?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Five five five, zero one four two, seven seven three one.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Five five five, zero one four two, seven seven three one. Is that correct?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. So if I understood correctly, you would like to report an experience your father had with one of our products. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Could you please tell me the name of the product?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I have the bottle here. Diclofenac Sodium. Seventy-five milligrams. It says delayed-release tablets.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Diclofenac Sodium seventy-five milligram delayed-release tablets. Thank you. And your father's name?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Harold Brennan.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And how old was Mr. Brennan?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: He was seventy-eight.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Please go ahead and tell me what happened, Ms. Brennan. Take your time.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. So he started the pills, um, about ten days before. And then on the Saturday he told me his stools were black. Like, black and tarry. He thought it was something he ate.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I see.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: And the next day, Sunday, he was throwing up blood. And he collapsed in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm so sorry. So first he had black stools, and the next day he vomited blood and collapsed. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And what happened after that?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: My mom called nine one one. The ambulance took him to St. Luke's Hospital. They admitted him straight to the ICU.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: He was admitted to the intensive care unit. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Did the doctors tell you what they found?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: They found a bleeding ulcer in his stomach. He had an endoscopy, and they gave him four units of blood.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. I apologize, I know this is difficult. Did any of the doctors say how serious it was at that time?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes, the ICU doctor told us it was life-threatening. She said that on the first night.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm very sorry. And how is, I mean, what happened after that?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: He held on for a few days. And he died on the ninth. October ninth.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm truly sorry, Ms. Brennan. Please take a moment if you need it.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: It's okay. Sorry. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Do you know what was given as the cause of death?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The death certificate says bleeding ulcer in the stomach. And it says upper G I hemorrhage. I think that's the medical word.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Bleeding ulcer in the stomach, upper G I hemorrhage. Thank you. I will document your father's experience with the medication. I have just a few quick questions to ask you. May I please proceed with those questions?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Could you please help me with when exactly your father started using the Diclofenac Sodium?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: September twenty-second. I picked it up for him, it's on the pharmacy receipt.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: September twenty-second. And how was he taking it, how many tablets and how often?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: One tablet twice a day. Morning and night. With breakfast and supper.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: One tablet twice a day. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And what was he taking it for?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: For his knees. He had osteoarthritis in both knees. It got really bad this year.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Osteoarthritis in both knees. And who prescribed the medication?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Doctor Okafor. His family doctor.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. When was the last time he took a tablet before he got sick?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The Saturday morning. The third. He took the morning one, and then he was in hospital.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: So his last dose was on the morning of the third. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And after he was admitted, was the medication stopped?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes, the hospital stopped it on the fourth, when he was admitted.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Was your father taking any other medications along with the Diclofenac Sodium?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes. Warfarin, for his heart. He had atrial fibrillation. And metoprolol.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Warfarin and metoprolol. Any others?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, that's all I can think of.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Did he have any medical conditions, like high blood pressure or diabetes?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: High blood pressure, yes. No diabetes. And the atrial fibrillation. And he had a stomach ulcer years ago, in twenty nineteen. It healed, though.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: High blood pressure, atrial fibrillation, and a stomach ulcer in twenty nineteen. Is that right?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's right.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Did any of the doctors at the hospital mention anything else that might have caused the bleeding?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: The doctor said the warfarin made the bleeding worse. Because it thins the blood.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I see. I will note that.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: But he'd been on warfarin for years, and he never had a problem. It was only after the new pills. Honestly, I think the new pills made the ulcer bleed.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I understand, Ms. Brennan. I will document that as your opinion. What about his height and weight?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Five foot nine. About one seventy-two pounds.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Five foot nine, one hundred seventy-two pounds. How about his ethnicity?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: White.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: And his date of birth?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: March fourteenth, nineteen forty-eight.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Would you like to share the physician details, like the name and telephone number?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Doctor Emeka Okafor, at Springfield Family Medicine. I don't have the number with me, sorry.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's completely fine. Would you like to share the pharmacy details from where you got the medication?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Walgreens on Main Street, in Springfield.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Would you have the prescription number?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Um, no. It's not on the bottle, I mean, I can't see it. No.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: No problem. Do you still have the bottle with you?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Could you please help me with the lot number? It is usually printed on the side of the label.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Lot R P four four seven one B, dash two.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: R P four four seven one B, dash two. And the expiry date?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: August twenty twenty-seven.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: August twenty twenty-seven. Thank you. And would you be able to read the N D C number? It is a ten-digit number near the barcode.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: One six five seven one, dash two zero one, dash zero six.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: One six five seven one, two zero one, zero six. Thank you. Ms. Brennan, would you like to share your email address?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure. Linda dot brennan five two at example dot com.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Linda dot brennan five two at example dot com. And do we have the permission to follow up with you, in case we need any additional information in the future?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes. That's fine. Call me on my cell.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. And would you like to share your mailing address for documentation purposes?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Eighty-eight Elm Street, Springfield, Illinois. Six two seven zero four.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Do you know if an autopsy was done?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, there wasn't one. The hospital said it wasn't needed.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you. Ms. Brennan, I just want to let you know that stomach bleeding is a known risk with this type of medicine, and it is listed in the prescribing information.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I will be sharing your report with our drug safety team, and a safety physician may contact you for more details.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. Nobody told him that. But okay.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm very sorry. I have made a note of everything. We do have a case reference number for future communications. Please note it down.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It's P V, two six one zero, one nine four four.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: P V two six one zero one nine four four.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Ms. Brennan, before we finish, I'd like to explain what happens with your report. It will be reviewed by a safety physician, and because it involves a death, it will be treated as a serious report.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It will be sent to the F D A within the required timelines. Your personal details are kept confidential.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. Thank you. That's good to know.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's right. Is there anything else I can help you with?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No. That was it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for calling, Ms. Brennan. Again, I'm very sorry for your loss. Take care. Goodbye.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Thank you. Bye.
